sources: University of California Statewide IPM Program, Brown Recluse and Other Recluse Spiders: 6 equal-sized eyes in 3 pairs; uniformly colored abdomen and legs, no leg spines, body no longer than 3/8 inch; the violin marking is not a reliable way to identify it; no populations in California; lives in the south central Midwest from southeastern Nebraska to southwestern Ohio, south through Texas to northern Georgia; nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt; found in storage boxes and under clutter, and at dawn may shelter in clothing or shoes; about 10% of bites cause moderate or greater tissue damage and scarring, the vast majority heal well without medical intervention; deaths reported in children are extremely rare; necrotic wounds are commonly misdiagnosed as brown recluse bites; shake out clothes and shoes, use sticky traps along floor boards, move the bed away from the wall; https://ipm.ucanr.edu/home-and-landscape/brown-recluse-and-other-recluse-spiders/

UC Riverside, Rick Vetter, How to Identify (and Misidentify) a Brown Recluse Spider: six eyes in pairs (one pair in front, one on either side), most spiders have eight; dark violin shape on the cephalothorax but not reliable for non-experts; uniformly light-colored legs, no stripes or bands; no spines on the legs; about 3/8 inch body length, longer than 1/2 inch is not a recluse; outside the range map it is highly unlikely you have one; https://spiders.ucr.edu/recluseid.html

Vetter & Barger 2002, Journal of Medical Entomology 39(6): 948-951, An infestation of 2,055 brown recluse spiders (Araneae: Sicariidae) and no envenomations in a Kansas home: 2,055 collected in six months (2001) from a home in Lenexa, Kansas, at least 400 large enough to envenomate, and no envenomations of the residents; https://doi.org/10.1603/0022-2585-39.6.948

beats.say: Number two. The brown recluse. By day, it hides in boxes, clothes, and shoes.
Its venom can kill the skin around its bite. About one bite in ten leaves a scar.
Six eyes, in three pairs. Legs all one plain color. No stripes, and no spines.
In one Kansas house, over two thousand were caught in six months. And nobody got bitten.
Most bites heal well, and many wounds blamed on a recluse are really something else.
Brown recluse. S tier. Rare bites, but real damage. One spot left.
